Claim: Having a main partner is beneficial for HIV-positive individuals.

Abstract (HIV-positive homosexual men and the role of male sex partners in the epidemic):
OBJECTIVES To explore the role of male sex partners in the HIV epidemic among HIV-positive homosexual men in France. DESIGN Cross-sectional study of HIV-positive homosexual men in France. SETTING HIV treatment and counseling centers in France. PARTICIPANTS 227 HIV-positive homosexual men in the Paris area. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES Number of new HIV infections per year, sexual risk behavior, and condom use. RESULTS Having a main partner was associated with a lower number of new HIV infections per year (1.2 vs. 2.7; p < 0.05), but a higher number of new infections per year per sex partner (0.3 vs. 0.5; p < 0.05), and decreased condom use (35% vs. 63%; p < 0.05). CONCLUSIONS Having a main partner may be associated with reduced sexual risk behavior but with an increased HIV transmission risk, due to more sex partners and less condom use.

Does this abstract support the claim (SUPPORTED) or contradict it (REFUTED)? Give only SUPPORTED or REFUTED on the ANSWER line.

ANSWER: REFUTED. The study suggests that having a main partner may lead to an increased risk of HIV transmission due to more sex partners and decreased condom use.

Confidence Level: High


Claim: HIV-positive individuals with a stable partnership have better treatment outcomes.

Abstract (Fidelity in HIV-infected individuals and the impact of fidelity on patient outcomes):
OBJECTIVES To investigate the role of fidelity in HIV treatment outcomes. DESIGN Cross-sectional study of HIV-infected individuals in the United States. SETTING HIV treatment centers in the United States. PARTICIPANTS 253 HIV-infected individuals. MAIN OUTCOME MEASURES Adherence to antiretroviral therapy and viral load suppression. RESULTS Higher rates of reported fidelity were significantly associated with better adherence to antiretroviral therapy and viral load suppression. CONCLUSIONS Having a faithful relationship is associated with better HIV treatment outcomes in terms of adherence to therapy and viral suppression.

Does this abstract support the claim (SUPPORTED) or contradict it (REFUTED)? Give only SUPPORTED or REFUTED on the ANSWER line.

ANSWER: SUPPORTED. The study found that higher rates of reported fidelity were associated with better HIV treatment outcomes.

Confidence Level: High
